title: IQ QUEST Battle Pool Medium B
creator: IQ QUEST · Powered by IQ Labs
theme: Fifteen independent medium battle puzzles, each with complete rules and no story dependencies. A fresh combination can challenge friends to beat your time.

levels.title: 01 · The Backwards Cipher
levels.q: First a word was shifted 7 letters FORWARD using the Caesar alphabet (Z wraps to A). Then the resulting string was REVERSED. The display now reads ZUVJHLI. Recover the original word.
levels.h: Undo the last operation first: reverse the displayed letters, then undo the forward shift.

levels.title: 02 · The Double Mirror
levels.q: An encoder first mirrors every letter using A↔Z, B↔Y, etc., then shifts each mirrored letter 4 places FORWARD (Z wraps to A). The final code is OJEESZ. Undo BOTH operations to recover the word.
levels.h: Reverse the Caesar shift before applying the mirror substitution.

levels.title: 03 · The Alternating Engine
levels.q: The sequence is 3, 7, 14, 18, 36, 40, ?. It alternates between ADD 4 and MULTIPLY BY 2, starting with addition. Find the NEXT value.
levels.h: Write the two different rules over alternating arrows; do not apply one rule every time.

levels.title: 04 · The Coordinate Map
levels.q: A 5×5 grid has rows and columns numbered 1 to 5. Start at (row 2, column 2). Follow W → S → E → S → W (N=−1 row, S=+1 row, E=+1 column, W=−1 column). Enter the final TWO-DIGIT code ROW then COLUMN, without punctuation.
levels.h: Track row and column separately. Do not turn the grid or swap the coordinate order.

levels.title: 05 · The 24-Hour Relay
levels.q: A 24-hour station clock shows 17:25. SUBTRACT 11:50 hours and minutes, wrapping at midnight. Enter the final time as HH:MM.
levels.h: Convert everything to minutes, adjust, then convert back to a 24-hour time.

levels.title: 06 · The Three Seals
levels.q: Three positive numbers A, B and C satisfy A+B=11, B+C=13, and A+C=14. What is A+B+C?
levels.h: Adding all three equations counts each unknown exactly twice.

levels.title: 07 · The Hexadecimal Message
levels.q: The lock stores ASCII letters as hexadecimal bytes: 47 41 54 45. Decode each byte to a capital letter (for example hex 41 means A). What four-letter word is hidden?
levels.h: Convert each two-digit hex byte separately; keep the resulting letters in order.

levels.title: 08 · Exactly One True
levels.q: A key lies under LEFT, MIDDLE or RIGHT. Exactly ONE of the following statements is true: (1) The key is NOT under RIGHT. (2) The key is under LEFT. (3) The key is NOT under LEFT. Which position has the key?
levels.h: For each possible position, mark each statement true or false. Keep only the position producing exactly one true claim.

levels.title: 09 · The Ordered Operations
levels.q: Start with 9, multiply by 5, add 13, and finally divide by 2. What exact number results?
levels.h: Keep the running result after each of the four specified operations.

levels.title: 10 · The Repeating Key
levels.q: A Vigenère encoder uses A=0 through Z=25 and repeats the key KEY. It encrypts each plain letter p as (p + key letter) mod 26. The ciphertext is FESVX. SUBTRACT the repeating key to recover the original five-letter word.
levels.h: Repeat the key under the ciphertext first, then subtract letter positions with wraparound.

levels.title: 11 · The Two-by-Two Seal
levels.q: The 2×2 matrix has first row [6, 3] and second row [5, 8]. Its determinant is (top-left × bottom-right) − (top-right × bottom-left). Calculate that determinant.
levels.h: Use the diagonal products and preserve the subtraction order.

levels.title: 12 · The Blocked Junction
levels.q: On a grid, travel from (0,0) to (5,3) using only RIGHT (+1 x) and UP (+1 y). You may NOT pass through (3,1). How many shortest paths are there?
levels.h: Count all unrestricted shortest paths, then subtract those that pass through the blocked junction.

levels.title: 13 · The Double Remainder
levels.q: Find the SMALLEST positive integer larger than 35 satisfying x mod 3 = 1 AND x mod 4 = 3. Enter the integer.
levels.h: List integers with one remainder, then test the second remainder on each candidate.

levels.title: 14 · The Two Machines
levels.q: Machine A makes 4 parts per minute and machine B makes 3 parts per minute. Both run together for 4 minutes, then A stops while B runs for 2 MORE minutes. How many parts were made in total?
levels.h: Separate the shared running time from B’s extra two minutes.

levels.title: 15 · The Two-Rail Cipher
levels.q: A six-letter word is written in a two-rail zigzag: letters at positions 1,3,5 go on the TOP rail; 2,4,6 on the BOTTOM. Then the TOP is followed by the BOTTOM, giving CPEIHR. Reverse this rail-fence cipher and recover the original word.
levels.h: Split the six letters into two groups of three, then interleave the two groups.
